newsitem.title: USA: US official-faster growth abroad to cut trade gap.
newsitem.headline: US official-faster growth abroad to cut trade gap.

text.p: Faster economic growth overseas is expected to help narrow the U.S. trade deficit this year, Commerce Department chief economist Lee Price said on Wednesday.
"While the dollar has some effects, recent history has shown that economic growth has a bigger effect on our trade balance," he told Reuters Financial Television.
He added that the dollar now is in about the same range that it has been for the last six to seven years.
Price said Canada's economy is expected to grow much faster this year than last. The outlook for European economies is also more optimistic, he said.
The Commerce Department reported earlier that the U.S. trade deficit rose 8.7 percent last year to $114.23 billion, the highest since 1988's $115.5 billion.

For December alone, the trade deficit rose 29.6 percent, to $10.29 billion. Price said the rise in the December deficit should not have much impact on gross domestic product data for the fourth quarter as Commerce had already factored such an increase into its initial estimate of fourth quarter growth.
That first estimate put growth in the fourth quarter at a hefty 4.7 percent in the forth quarter. Commerce is scheduled to issue a revised GDP estimate on Feb. 28.
